title: Haloumi and Samosa-Style Hash
subtitle: with Spinach and Raisins
description: You may notice this recipe's back for a victory lap – that's because sometimes you can't beat a tried-and-true winner! Our Dinnerly home cooks loved this recipe, so here it is again for you to enjoy its easy cooking, big flavours and satisfying goodness.

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Peel the sweet potatoes and cut into 2cm chunks. Thinly slice the onion. Slice the haloumi.

Cook veggies: Put the sweet potato in a medium saucepan of cold salted water and bring to the boil. Cook for 10 mins, then add the peas and cook for a further 2-3 mins until the sweet potato and peas are tender. Drain.

Saute onion: Meanwhile, heat 1 tbs vegetable oil in a medium deep frypan over medium heat. Cook the onion, stirring, for 3 mins or until softened. Add the curry powder and sweet potato and peas and cook, stirring, for 1-2 mins until fragrant.

Add spinach: Add the spinach, raisins and 1 tbs water to the veggie mixture and cook, stirring, for 1-2 mins until the spinach is wilted. Remove the pan from the heat. Taste, then season with salt and pepper.

Cook haloumi and serve up: Heat 2 tsp vegetable oil in a medium frypan over medium-high heat. Cook the haloumi for 2 mins each side or until golden. Remove from the pan. Divide the veggie hash among plates, top with the haloumi and enjoy!

Did you know?: We've used traditional Indian samosas as inspiration for this dish. Samosas are triangle-shaped pastries filled with a mixture of spiced veggies (often potato and peas), with some versions including meat. Once filled, the pastries are deep-fried until golden and crisp.
